nodes.name: Experiment
nodes.definition: Intentionally disturbing a system by changing factors, to learn cause and effect.

nodes.name: Run
nodes.definition: One experiment in a set: eight experiments are eight runs.

nodes.name: Response
nodes.definition: The measured outcome of a run, written y. It must always be measurable in some way.

nodes.name: Qualitative outcome
nodes.definition: An outcome described in categories, such as pass or fail, or a colour.

nodes.name: Objective
nodes.definition: An outcome together with what you want of it: maximize, minimize, or keep the same.

nodes.name: Factor
nodes.definition: The thing you can change to influence the outcome.

nodes.name: Numeric factor
nodes.definition: A factor with ordered, measured values, such as 15 mL or 30 mL of water.

nodes.name: Categorical factor
nodes.definition: A factor with a few values that have no order, such as soil A or soil B.

nodes.name: Level
nodes.definition: A setting of a factor in a design, such as its low (-1) or high (+1) value.

nodes.name: Cause and effect
nodes.definition: A change in a factor that produces a change in the response; shown only by intentional manipulation.

nodes.name: Happenstance data
nodes.definition: Everyday operating data, collected without intentional changes; it cannot show cause and effect.

nodes.name: Feedback control
nodes.definition: Control systems keep operation in a small zone, so the data they produce carry little information.

nodes.name: Correlation
nodes.definition: Two variables moving together: necessary, but not sufficient, for causality.

nodes.name: Learning cycle
nodes.definition: Conjecture, expected consequences, experiment and data, then a new or revised conjecture.

nodes.name: Conjecture
nodes.definition: A hypothesis believed true, whose consequences an experiment tests.

nodes.name: Troubleshooting
nodes.definition: Experimenting to fix a problem, which also teaches you about the system.

nodes.name: Disturbance
nodes.definition: A variable that affects y but is not of interest: operators, ambient conditions, equipment, lab analyses, time.

nodes.name: Controlled disturbance
nodes.definition: A disturbance held constant for all runs, so its effect cancels out.

nodes.name: Time-dependent effect
nodes.definition: Slow changes such as catalyst deactivation or fouling that affect the response over time.

nodes.name: Randomization
nodes.definition: Running experiments in random order so unknown disturbances cannot systematically affect the response.

nodes.name: Independence
nodes.definition: The assumption behind t-based confidence intervals; randomization guarantees it.

nodes.name: Randomization test
nodes.definition: Compare the observed difference with the differences from every possible reassignment of the A and B labels.

nodes.name: Pairing
nodes.definition: Running two experiments on the same subject and analysing their difference, so a shared disturbance cancels.

nodes.name: Comparing two conditions
nodes.definition: Comparing condition A with B using a pooled variance and a confidence interval for the difference.

nodes.name: Pooled variance
nodes.definition: A combined variance estimate from two groups, used in the z-value for their difference.

nodes.name: Indicator variable
nodes.definition: A 0/1 variable that codes condition A or B in a least squares model.

nodes.name: Confidence interval
nodes.definition: A range for an effect; the effect is statistically significant when the interval does not span zero.

nodes.name: t-distribution
nodes.definition: The reference distribution for a difference or a coefficient divided by its standard error.

nodes.name: Null hypothesis
nodes.definition: The assumption that there is no difference between A and B.

nodes.name: Statistical significance
nodes.definition: An effect larger than the noise, judged by its confidence interval.

nodes.name: Practical significance
nodes.definition: Whether an effect is large enough to matter, judged from the interval's width and the process variance.

nodes.name: Changing one single variable at a time
nodes.definition: Changing one factor at a time: an inefficient way to experiment that can stop at a suboptimal point.

nodes.name: False optimum
nodes.definition: A point that looks best when factors are changed one at a time, but is not the optimum.

nodes.name: Order dependence
nodes.definition: With COST the result depends on which factor is changed first.

nodes.name: Designed experiment
nodes.definition: A planned set of runs that changes several factors together, in random order, so the result does not depend on run order.

nodes.name: Full factorial
nodes.definition: Every combination of the factors' two levels: 2^k runs for k factors.

nodes.name: Coding
nodes.definition: Centering and scaling a factor: (value - center)/(range/2), so low is -1 and high is +1.

nodes.name: Standard order
nodes.definition: Writing runs with the first factor's sign alternating fastest and the last slowest.

nodes.name: Choosing the factor range
nodes.definition: Choose low and high at the edges of normal operation, not at the extreme values a factor could take.

nodes.name: Cube plot
nodes.definition: The design drawn as a square or cube with the response written at each corner.

nodes.name: Main effect
nodes.definition: The average change in y when a factor moves from its low to its high level.

nodes.name: Interaction
nodes.definition: When the effect of one factor depends on the level of another. Interactions are symmetric.

nodes.name: Two-factor interaction
nodes.definition: The interaction of two factors, such as T x S.

nodes.name: Three-factor interaction
nodes.definition: The interaction of three factors; seldom large in real systems.

nodes.name: Interaction plot
nodes.definition: The response against one factor, a line per level of another; lines that are not parallel show interaction.

nodes.name: Effect over half the range
nodes.definition: This book reports an effect as the change over half the factor's range; Box, Hunter and Hunter report double.

nodes.name: Least squares model
nodes.definition: y = Xb + e, fitted with b = (X'X)^-1 X'y. It works even when the design was not run exactly as planned.

nodes.name: Model matrix X
nodes.definition: One row per run and one column per model term, with a column of ones for the intercept.

nodes.name: Orthogonality
nodes.definition: The columns of X are independent, so X'X is diagonal and each coefficient is estimated and read on its own.

nodes.name: Intercept
nodes.definition: The model's constant b0; for a coded factorial, the average of the runs and the predicted center point.

nodes.name: Coefficient
nodes.definition: The change in y for a one-unit change in a coded factor, that is, over half its range.

nodes.name: Keep the parent main effects
nodes.definition: If an interaction is significant, keep in the model every main effect that it is made of.

nodes.name: Read main effects with their interactions
nodes.definition: A main effect cannot be interpreted on its own when it takes part in a significant interaction.

nodes.name: Robustness
nodes.definition: A small effect means y is insensitive to that factor: y is robust to changes in it.

nodes.name: Degrees of freedom
nodes.definition: Runs minus estimated parameters; needed to estimate the standard error.

nodes.name: Replicate
nodes.definition: A complete repeat of a run: setup, running the experiment and measuring the result.

nodes.name: Repeat measurement
nodes.definition: Measuring one sample twice; it estimates only measurement error and is not a true replicate.

nodes.name: Center point
nodes.definition: A run with every factor at coded 0. It tests curvature and adds degrees of freedom without breaking orthogonality.

nodes.name: Standard error
nodes.definition: The noise estimate from the residuals; for a coefficient, SE(b) = sqrt(S_E^2 / sum x^2).

nodes.name: Pareto plot
nodes.definition: Absolute coefficients in sorted order, intercept left out; significance judged by eye. Needs coded factors.

nodes.name: Significance from standard errors
nodes.definition: Report each effect with its standard error; it is significant when effect +/- c_t x SE excludes zero.

nodes.name: Refit without small effects
nodes.definition: Drop clearly small effects to gain degrees of freedom, then estimate the error and check the residuals.

nodes.name: Residual analysis
nodes.definition: Residuals plotted in run order, against fitted values, and on a q-q plot.

nodes.name: Factorial efficiency
nodes.definition: A factorial estimates a main effect with half the variance of COST: each observation works twice.

nodes.name: Missing values
nodes.definition: Lost responses. Drop high-order terms so the model can still be fitted by least squares.

nodes.name: Off-target run
nodes.definition: A run set to a level other than planned. Code its actual value and fit by least squares; X is then almost orthogonal.

nodes.name: Fractional factorial
nodes.definition: A fraction of a full factorial: 2^(k-p) runs for k factors.

nodes.name: Half fraction
nodes.definition: Half of a full factorial: 2^(k-1) runs.

nodes.name: Quarter fraction
nodes.definition: A quarter of a full factorial: 2^(k-2) runs.

nodes.name: Complementary half fraction
nodes.definition: The other half of a full factorial, made by flipping the sign of the generator.

nodes.name: Saturated design
nodes.definition: A design with one run per estimated term, such as 7 factors in 8 runs; usually resolution III.

nodes.name: Plackett-Burman design
nodes.definition: A screening design in any multiple of 4 runs from 12: 12, 16, 20, 24, ...

nodes.name: Confounding
nodes.definition: Two effects cannot be separated, so their coefficient estimates their sum.

nodes.name: Alias
nodes.definition: An effect confounded with another: A is an alias of BC.

nodes.name: Alias structure
nodes.definition: The list of aliases of every effect in a design.

nodes.name: Collinearity
nodes.definition: Identical columns in X, so X'X cannot be inverted.

nodes.name: Generator
nodes.definition: Assigning an extra factor to an interaction column, such as D = ABC.

nodes.name: Word
nodes.definition: A product of factor letters equal to I, such as ABD.

nodes.name: Defining relation
nodes.definition: All the words equal to I, found from the products of the generators: 2^p words.

nodes.name: Identity column I
nodes.definition: The column of ones. Any factor times itself is I.

nodes.name: Finding aliases
nodes.definition: Multiply an effect by the defining relation to list what it is aliased with.

nodes.name: Reassign factors to letters
nodes.definition: Choose which real factor gets which letter to obtain the least harmful confounding.

nodes.name: Resolution
nodes.definition: The length of the shortest word in the defining relation, written as a Roman numeral.

nodes.name: Resolution III
nodes.definition: Main effects are aliased with two-factor interactions. Good for screening.

nodes.name: Resolution IV
nodes.definition: Main effects are clear of two-factor interactions, which are aliased with each other. Good for characterizing.

nodes.name: Resolution V
nodes.definition: Two-factor interactions are clear of each other. Good for optimizing.

nodes.name: Trade-off table
nodes.definition: Resolution against number of factors and runs (Box, Hunter and Hunter, p 272).

nodes.name: Projectivity
nodes.definition: A design of resolution R contains a full factorial in any R - 1 factors.

nodes.name: Foldover
nodes.definition: Running a second fraction with signs switched, then analysing both fractions together.

nodes.name: Single-factor foldover
nodes.definition: Switch the signs of one factor to de-alias it and its two-factor interactions.

nodes.name: Full foldover
nodes.definition: Switch all signs to raise a resolution III design to resolution IV.

nodes.name: Sequential experimentation
nodes.definition: Experiments are run in stages, each designed from what the last one revealed.

nodes.name: Screening
nodes.definition: Finding the few important factors among many candidates.

nodes.name: Few large effects
nodes.definition: Main effects matter most, then two-factor interactions; three-factor interactions are seldom large.

nodes.name: Blocking
nodes.definition: Running the experiment in groups so a known disturbance affects the response without misleading the results.

nodes.name: Block
nodes.definition: A group of runs made under one level of a disturbance, such as one batch of material. Runs within a block are randomized.

nodes.name: Block generator
nodes.definition: The interaction the block effect is confounded with, such as block = ABC.

nodes.name: Block on the highest interaction
nodes.definition: Confound the block effect with the highest-order interaction, which is expected to be small.

nodes.name: Response surface methods
nodes.definition: A sequential way to move a process towards its optimum by fitting and climbing local models.

nodes.name: Response surface
nodes.definition: The unknown surface of y over the factors' space.

nodes.name: Steepest ascent
nodes.definition: Move all factors together in proportion to their coefficients: delta x_i = (b_i / b_A) delta x_A.

nodes.name: Steepest descent
nodes.definition: Steepest ascent in the opposite direction, to minimize y.

nodes.name: Step size
nodes.definition: Big enough to change the response in a few runs, small enough not to jump over the optimum.

nodes.name: Return to the last best point
nodes.definition: When the response drops, go back to the best run and fit a new factorial around it.

nodes.name: Curvature
nodes.definition: A bend in the response surface; every optimum has it, and a linear model cannot describe it.

nodes.name: Checking for curvature
nodes.definition: Compare the model's predicted center point, b0, with the measured center point.

nodes.name: Quadratic model
nodes.definition: A model with squared terms such as b_TT x_T^2, to describe curvature.

nodes.name: Central composite design
nodes.definition: A factorial plus center points plus axial points; fits a quadratic model.

nodes.name: Axial point
nodes.definition: A run on one factor's axis, (2^k)^0.25 coded units from the center: 1.41 for 2 factors, 1.68 for 3.

nodes.name: Box-Behnken design
nodes.definition: A three-level design for quadratic models, named as another design to research.

nodes.name: Contour plot
nodes.definition: Lines of equal predicted response, used to choose where to run next.

nodes.name: Optimum
nodes.definition: The settings with the best response. The surface is flat there.

nodes.name: Response levels off
nodes.definition: Successive steps give little improvement.

nodes.name: Two equal steps
nodes.definition: The response stays about the same for two steps: you have jumped over the optimum.

nodes.name: Response drops
nodes.definition: The response falls, sometimes fast, after a step: you overshot the optimum.

nodes.name: Interactions as large as main effects
nodes.definition: Interaction terms similar to or larger than the main effects.

nodes.name: Center point far from prediction
nodes.definition: The measured center point differs from b0 by much more than the noise.

nodes.name: Near an optimum
nodes.definition: The region where the surface bends, so a linear model no longer points the way.

nodes.name: Several responses
nodes.definition: Two or more outcomes that trade off, such as production rate and energy.

nodes.name: Combine into one response
nodes.definition: Rewrite the outcomes as one y, such as total cost or net profit.

nodes.name: Overlay the response surfaces
nodes.definition: Superimpose the contours of each response so the trade-offs can be seen.

nodes.name: Categorical factors in RSM
nodes.definition: Fix a categorical factor, optimize the rest, then try its other value.

nodes.name: Evolutionary operation
nodes.definition: Small, repeated factorial perturbations on a full-scale process to keep it at its moving optimum.

nodes.name: Process drift
nodes.definition: The optimum moves as heat exchangers foul, catalyst deactivates, and raw materials change.

nodes.name: Phase 1: screening
nodes.definition: Put as many factors as possible into as few runs as possible, with a saturated or Plackett-Burman design.

nodes.name: Phase 2: sequential runs
nodes.definition: Add runs to the first ones: foldover, projectivity, and fractions of higher resolution.

nodes.name: Phase 3: optimization
nodes.definition: Explore the response surface of the important factors, then add curvature terms near the optimum.

nodes.name: Phase 4: maintain the optimum
nodes.definition: Keep hunting for the moving optimum with evolutionary operation.

nodes.name: Spend 25% first
nodes.definition: Spend no more than 20% to 25% of time and budget on the first group of experiments.

nodes.name: The best time to run an experiment
nodes.definition: The best time to run an experiment is after the experiment: you always learn what you wish you had done.

nodes.name: Run the center point first
nodes.definition: The first run often fails while you learn the protocol; make it a center point, which the analysis does not need.

nodes.name: Constraint
nodes.definition: A region where the process may not operate, for safety or physical reasons.

nodes.name: Lost orthogonality
nodes.definition: Moving a run to obey a constraint makes X no longer orthogonal and shrinks the region the design spans.

nodes.name: Optimal design
nodes.definition: Runs chosen by a computer to optimize a criterion, for a model you specify, subject to constraints.

nodes.name: Candidate set
nodes.definition: Every allowed combination of factor levels, from which an optimal design picks its runs.

nodes.name: Candidate exchange algorithm
nodes.definition: Swap candidate points into and out of the design until the criterion is best.

nodes.name: Optimality criterion
nodes.definition: The quantity an optimal design optimizes, such as the determinant of X'X.

nodes.name: D-optimality
nodes.definition: Maximize det(X'X): minimize the general variance of the parameters.

nodes.name: A-optimality
nodes.definition: Minimize trace((X'X)^-1): the average variance of the parameters.

nodes.name: G-optimality
nodes.definition: Minimize the maximum variance of the predictions.

nodes.name: V-optimality
nodes.definition: Minimize the average variance of the predictions.

nodes.name: Specify the model first
nodes.definition: An optimal design needs the model before the runs; in a factorial the model is implicit.

nodes.name: Adding runs to a design
nodes.definition: Add the runs that most improve the criterion, for example most increase det(X'X), to fix or extend a design.

nodes.name: Definitive screening design
nodes.definition: A three-level screening design, a type of optimal design, that can also estimate second-order effects.

nodes.name: Mixture design
nodes.definition: A design for components whose proportions add to 100%.

nodes.name: Proportions sum to one
nodes.definition: Mixture components cannot change independently, because sum x_i = 1.

nodes.name: Simplex
nodes.definition: The triangular region of a three-component mixture: pure components at the corners.

nodes.name: Bioreactor by COST
nodes.definition: Changing temperature then substrate one at a time stops at 69.5% yield, short of the optimum.

nodes.name: The lady tasting tea
nodes.definition: Fisher's illustration of randomization: is her score better than chance?

nodes.name: Brittleness in TK104 and TK107
nodes.definition: The randomization test (79.6%) and the t-test (79.3%) agree.

nodes.name: Conversion vs T and S
nodes.definition: A 2^2 factorial in temperature and substrate: y = 61.5 - 5 x_T - 3 x_S - 0.5 x_T x_S.

nodes.name: Washing hands
nodes.definition: Hot water enhances soap, and soap enhances hot water: an interaction.

nodes.name: Pollutant from a molding plant
nodes.definition: A 2^3 factorial in chemical, temperature and stirring; a large chemical x speed interaction.

nodes.name: Yield, pressure and impurity
nodes.definition: Pressure correlates with yield only because operators raise it when impurity causes froth.

nodes.name: Seven factors in eight runs
nodes.definition: A 2^(7-4) design with D = AB, E = AC, F = BC, G = ABC; A, C and G matter.

nodes.name: Eight factors in 16 runs
nodes.definition: A 2^(8-4) design of resolution IV.

nodes.name: Two batches of raw material
nodes.definition: A 2^3 factorial split into two blocks of 4, with the batch confounded with ABC.

nodes.name: Climbing to maximum profit
nodes.definition: Factorials, steepest ascent and a central composite design find the profit optimum near 343 K and 1.6 g/L.

nodes.name: Fruit punch mixture
nodes.definition: The cheapest blend that still tastes right, with a region of high acidity excluded.

nodes.name: Cell-culture bioreactor
nodes.definition: Five factors at 10 days a run: a full factorial would take almost a year.

nodes.name: Which of eight factors matter?
nodes.definition: Narrow a list of plausible factors and rank their effects.

nodes.name: Three factors left: what next?
nodes.definition: How to run the rest of the experiments after screening.

nodes.name: What do these old results show?
nodes.definition: Interpret existing experimental data and choose where to operate.

nodes.name: Long shelf life with less energy?
nodes.definition: Find settings that keep one outcome good while improving another.

nodes.name: High temperature and pressure together are unsafe
nodes.definition: Plan an experiment when part of the region cannot be run.

nodes.name: R. A. Fisher, The Design of Experiments
nodes.definition: The source of randomization and of factorial experimentation, from the 1930s.

nodes.name: Box, Hunter and Hunter, Statistics for Experimenters
nodes.definition: The main reference for this chapter.

nodes.name: Box and Hunter, 2^(k-p) fractional factorial designs (1961)
nodes.definition: The papers that set out fractional factorials and resolution.

nodes.name: Box, Evolutionary operation (1957)
nodes.definition: The paper that introduced evolutionary operation.

nodes.name: St. John and Draper, D-optimality (1975)
nodes.definition: A review of D-optimal designs.

nodes.name: Jones and Nachtsheim, definitive screening (2011)
nodes.definition: The paper that introduced definitive screening designs.
